page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 vCPUs sourced from 8 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. CPU features include AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16) along with AES cryptography and bit-manipulation instructions. Memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate high single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 2,866.0, ranking in the top tier alongside a stress-ng single-core score of 3,779.7. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 41.9 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression delivered 18.27 GB/sec, placing both in the top tier. Multi-core performance aligns with expected 16-vCPU capacity, recording 15,465.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 30,202.82 in stress-ng multi-core. In memory workloads, uncached large-block read operations achieved 51.56 GB/sec while write operations reached 34.17 GB/sec, supporting a strong PassMark memory score of 2,814.87.

For specialized execution, the instance displays strong efficiency on compact models and text processing tasks. Geekbench text processing scored 3,800.0, placing in the top tier. In CPU-based LLM inference, text generation using a small 135M parameter model clocked 404.55 tokens/sec, and prompt processing reached 2,569.77 tokens/sec. Performance drops to middle-tier tiers on medium 7B models (13.07 tokens/sec generation) and bottom-tier throughput on 70B models (5.5 tokens/sec prompt processing), reflecting the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. Database operations via PassMark registered 10,016.84 alongside Redis throughput of 26.92 million SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the E16as_v7 lies in the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and lack of GPU acceleration, which necessitates external managed disks for persistence and caps deep learning model scales. However, with its 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and robust single-core compute performance, the configuration presents strong qualitative cost efficiency for high-memory requirements. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise backend applications, data manipulation pipelines, and high-throughput compression tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E16as_v7 is a memory-optimized instance running on the AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. It features 16 vCPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores, backed by 128.0 GB of system memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote persistent disks. In benchmark evaluations, the E16as_v7 exhibits top-tier single-core compute, text processing, and decompression throughput, while maintaining mid-range multi-core and database execution profiles. CPU-based inference executes efficiently on lightweight models, though performance drops significantly on larger architectures without accelerator hardware. With balanced memory density and high frequency cores, the E16as_v7 is well suited for in-memory caching systems, Redis databases, enterprise application servers, and data preprocessing pipelines.
